fatal_errors: The proposed ligand-controlled thermal-shock route does not reconstruct the spray-dried precursor and low-temperature H2 decomposition-reduction intervention.

The mechanism omits preferential reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru, hydrogen dissociation and spillover-assisted reduction of base metals, and incorporation into the initially established noble-metal lattice.
It misses the central crystal-selection mechanism in Pt-Ru systems: kinetic retention of Pt-fcc followed by thermally activated fcc-to-hcp conversion as Ru content and reheating temperature increase.
The cited evidence does not support tailored organic ligands or a 150–200 °C cooling hold; one citation instead emphasizes extremely rapid cooling to suppress secondary phases.
Ligand addition and cooling history are changed simultaneously, so the proposed experiment cannot identify which intervention governs any observed improvement.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad challenge of kinetically suppressing segregation in multielement nanoparticles and proposes measurable structural outcomes, but it describes a substantially different synthesis regime and governing mechanism. The target uses compositionally homogeneous spray-dried salt particles, gradual heating in H2 to about 300 °C, and noble-metal-dependent reduction chemistry. Pt, Ir, or Ru first establish an fcc or hcp lattice and catalyze hydrogen-assisted reduction of neighboring transition-metal salts; Pd and noble-metal-free controls fail. Crystal selection in Pt-Ru alloys is then governed by composition and thermally activated fcc-to-hcp transformation during 400–500 °C reheating. None of these discriminating features appears in the generated account. Its predicted single-phase formation and reduced segregation are directionally relevant but generic, and it omits the Pt-black catalytic benchmark, methanol-oxidation outcome, Pd and noble-metal-free controls, and composition-dependent Pt-Ru phase boundaries. The proposed measurements could test phase homogeneity, but a factorial design separating ligand presence from cooling protocol would be required. Overall, the ligand/hold mechanism is conceivable as an alternative hypothesis, yet the supplied evidence only supports limited mobility and rapid thermal processing in general and does not validate the specific intervention or mechanism.
